newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia econ institute urges slower wage growth.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia econ institute urges slower wage growth.

text.p: Slovenia's top government economic institute said on Wednesday wage growth should ease to three percent this year from 5.1 percent in 1996 so the country could meet its output growth target of four percent this year.

"A slowdown of the growth of salaries is urgent, therefore we believe the consensus reached this week was necessary," Janez Potocnik, head of the Institute of Macroeconomic Analysis and Development, told a news conference.
Slovenian employers and a majority of the country's labour unions on Monday signed a new collective agreement on work benefits aimed at putting a lid on excessive wage growth.
The institute said wage growth should not exceed 2.5 percent in 1998 in order for the country to meet the 1998 gross domestic product (GDP) growth target of 4.5 percent.
Slower wage growth is expected to contribute to a 0.5 percent employment growth in 1998, while no significant changes in employment are expected this year, the institute said.
March unemployment eased to 14.4 percent from 14.5 percent in February but was significantly above the 13.9 percent registered in March of last year.

The institute also said GDP per capita was expected to grow to $10,434 in 1998 from $9,058 in 1997 and $9,320 in 1996. It said the 1997 figure was expected to be pushed down by the strength of the dollar. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
